full_text: 9 years, 9 months, 9 days. That's how long he went without losing. His name is Edwin Moses. His college had no running track, so he trained at public high schools while finishing a physics degree. Before March 1976 he had run exactly one 400 meter hurdles race in his life; four months later he was Olympic champion. In August 1977 he lost, in Berlin. And then he simply stopped losing. The streak: 122 consecutive races, 107 consecutive finals, four world records, gold in Montreal and Los Angeles. Even the 1980 boycott, which took a whole Olympics from him mid-streak, couldn't put a loss on the record. It took until June 1987, in Madrid, for anyone to beat him again. He responded by winning his next ten races in a row.
